title: Grateful Dead Live at Clark University on 1969-04-20
lineage: SBD > Cassette Master (Ampex C-90, no Dolby) > DAT(M)@ 44.1K via Panasonic SV3700>DAT(1)>DAT(2) > WAV via Sony SDT9000 DDS drive using VDAT0.6f  > Soundforge 4.0

ai_review.summary: A historically treasured April 20 1969 Clark University show with a soaring Dark Star and Mountains of the Moon, captured on an audience tape that’s hissy and low‑volume but still listenable.
ai_review.review: The performance is celebrated for its magical early‑Dead vibe – Dark Star, Mountains of the Moon, Death Don't Have No Mercy and Doin’ That Rag are repeatedly highlighted as standout moments.  The recording is an audience source with noticeable hiss, muffiness and a bad cut on Eleven, yet fans find it sufficiently clear to enjoy the night’s mellow improvisations and Jerry’s dominant vocals and guitar work.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews give consistent praise for the show’s musical moments while noting similar technical flaws (hiss, low volume).  The strong positive weighting of the performance outweighs the recording shortcomings.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Low overall level, noticeable hiss and occasional mud; a bad edit on Eleven.  Some listeners report this version is less hissy than other copies, but the tape remains imperfect.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First night of an epic four‑night run; the set is described as mellow yet magical, with strong improvisational passages and a memorable Dark Star that sits at the heart of the evening.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is praised (sweet, dominant vocals, tuning intro before Morning Dew) and his vocal performance is called “great” and “heavy lifting”.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for rhythm work and occasional vocal moments; no specific instrumental critique.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pig" McKernan (referred to as Pig) receives a nod for holding court with a schoolgirl during the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart is mentioned in anecdotes about backstage drama; overall drum work is not directly critiqued but implied solid.
